title: The Halls of Ivy
paragraphs: A warm campus comedy starring Ronald and Benita Colman as college president Dr. William Todhunter Hall and his wife Victoria, mixing academic problems, student life, and domestic humor.
Campus situation comedy centered on Ivy College president Dr. William Todhunter Hall and his wife Victoria.

The run breaks into several distinct periods: Audition recordings (June 22, 1949 to June 23, 1949) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], NBC/Schlitz radio run (January 6, 1950 to June 25, 1952) on [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], and Television continuation represented by soundtrack audio (October 26, 1954 to June 14, 1955).

Names that turn up again and again in the surviving run include Don Quinn (creator and writer), [[person|benita-hume|Benita Hume]] (performer), [[person|ronald-colman|Ronald Colman]] (performer and writer), Ken Carpenter (announcer and performer), Henry Russell (composer, conductor, and music), Nat Wolff (director, performer, and producer), and Herb Butterfield (performer).

Across its run, the surviving broadcasts are tied to [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]], [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]], and [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]].

The stories often return to college and higher education, students and student life, faculty and academic work, marriage and domestic partnership, college administration and governance, and college sports.
The show also sits in a wider radio history that includes Postwar college and campus life in radio comedy, Schlitz sponsorship of prestige radio comedy, and Radio-to-television continuation.

If you are following the same actors and creative circles, related programs worth opening next include [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]], [[show|the-railroad-hour|The Railroad Hour]], [[show|screen-directors-playhouse|Screen Directors Playhouse]], [[show|broadway-is-my-beat|Broadway Is My Beat]], and [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]].
